title: PorMe: A validated open-source image-based pore size and porosity measurement tool for 3D-printed structures
author: Contreras Raggio, Pardo, et al.

All acquired data were first preprocessed by filtering the parameters with a collinearity bigger than 0.8. steps.title: Acquire scaffold images
steps.instruction: Capture high‑resolution pictures of the 3‑D‑printed scaffold either while printing or immediately after printing, ensuring the entire inner geometry is visible.

steps.title: Run PorMe analysis
steps.instruction: Execute the PorMe Python algorithm on the acquired images to automatically measure strut thickness (Ss), strut spacing, and individual pore sizes for all visible pores.

steps.title: Define region of interest
steps.instruction: Select the red‑shaded region of interest (ROI) shown in Fig. 6 for each local segment of the scaffold; this ROI will be used for subsequent porosity calculations.

steps.title: Calculate local porosity (Eq 2)
steps.instruction: For each ROI, compute porosity using Porosity(%) = 100 × (1 – (Ss² × π) / (4 × Lh × Sd)), where Lh = 0.4 mm (designed layer height) and Sd = 0.8 mm (designed strut distance).

steps.title: Simplify porosity equation (Eq 3)
steps.instruction: Apply the numeric values of Lh and Sd to obtain Porosity(%) = 100 – 245.44 × Ss² (Ss in mm). Calculate this value for every segment and average the results to obtain the overall scaffold porosity.

steps.title: Predict porosity with ML model
steps.instruction: Use the previously trained linear model (LassoCV, CV = 5, α = 0.15) to predict porosity from pore size alone: Porosity(%) = 190.92 × Poresize – 17.94. The model was built on 70 % of the data (parameters: pore size, height, diameter) with R² = 0.81 (training) and R² = 0.86 (test).

steps.title: Generate pore‑size histogram
steps.instruction: Create a frequency distribution histogram for all measured pores (≈ 300 000 pores). Mark the mode at 360 µm and, if desired, overlay the designed pore size.

steps.title: Group histograms by material parameters
steps.instruction: Separate the pore‑size histograms according to ink preparation method (acetone = ACE, dichloromethane = DCM, mechanical compounding = MINI, control PCL = PCL), bio‑glass (BG) content, and extrusion temperature (°C).

steps.title: Perform circularity analysis
steps.instruction: Calculate the circularity of each pore for every printed layer, plot the cumulative mean circularity and its standard deviation across layers, and compare to the ideal square value (~0.785). Note the high variation within the first 10 layers.
